theophylline_apriori.headline_note: The headline is the PRE-SPECIFIED permeability declared in THEOPHYLLINE_PHYSCHEM before any result was computed. The sweep is reported in full so the sensitivity to that inferred input is visible. `best_by_cmax_aafe` is post-hoc selection and must not be quoted as the benchmark result.

dataset.name: Theophylline oral pharmacokinetics (Theoph)
dataset.license_note: Distributed in the R `datasets` package under GPL-2 | GPL-3. Redistributed unmodified by SYNTHBODY under those terms.
dataset.provenance: Obtained programmatically from the Rdatasets CSV mirror of R datasets::Theoph on 2026-10-12. 132 rows, 12 subjects, 11 observations each. No values were transcribed by hand and none were altered.
dataset.description: Twelve subjects each given a single oral dose of theophylline, with plasma concentrations measured at 11 time points over roughly 25 hours. The canonical teaching and benchmarking dataset for one-compartment first-order-absorption population pharmacokinetics.
known_limitations: Single dose only: provides no information about accumulation or time-varying clearance.
Healthy adults; the dataset carries no information about hepatic impairment, age extremes or drug interactions.
Only body weight is recorded as a covariate. Smoking status, which strongly affects theophylline clearance via CYP1A2, is not available.
Two subjects have a non-zero concentration recorded at nominal time zero, which a model with an absorption depot starting empty cannot reproduce.
Bioavailability is not identifiable from oral-only data, so clearance and volume estimated from it are apparent values (CL/F and V/F).

disposition_source.note: Estimated from the CALIBRATION subjects only by SYNTHBODY's two-stage fit. Because AUC is approximately dose*fabs/CL, the AUC metric is partly determined by this fit and is therefore the weakest of the three.

intrinsic_solubility_mg_per_mL.source: PubChem CID 2153: water solubility 7360 mg/L at 25 C. Public domain.

pka_acidic.source: PubChem CID 2153 dissociation constant, pKa = 8.81. Public domain.

effective_permeability_cm_per_s.source: NOT a retrieved measurement. Theophylline is a BCS Class I compound (high solubility, high permeability) and is essentially completely absorbed. A value above roughly 2-4e-4 cm/s is the conventional high-permeability threshold for human jejunal Peff. Lennernas's measured human Peff dataset (PMID 9548891) is paywalled and was not retrieved. Because this value is inferred rather than measured, the benchmark sweeps it across a plausible range instead of relying on a single number.

particle_radius_um.source: The Theoph dataset does not record the formulation. 25 um is a typical immediate-release particle radius and is a SYNTHBODY default. For a freely soluble drug the prediction is insensitive to it, which the benchmark checks.

theophylline_apriori.interpretation: tmax is the cleanest a-priori test: it is set by gastric emptying and small-intestinal transit, both taken from an open-access physiology source, and by permeability. Cmax is next. AUC is weakest because the disposition parameters were fitted to this drug (though to different subjects).
theophylline_apriori.honest_scope: This is a one-drug, one-formulation, highly-soluble-compound benchmark. It is NOT comparable to the Sjogren et al. benchmark, which deliberately used 12 drugs chosen for INCOMPLETE absorption — the regime where dissolution and solubility limitation dominate and where absorption models actually differ. A good result here says the machinery works; it says nothing about performance on poorly soluble compounds.

orbito_comparison.published_results_provenance: AAFE values as stated in the publicly available PubMed abstract of Sjögren et al. 2016 (PMID 26926043), covering 12 drugs and 44 oral administrations. These are RECORDED values for specific 2016 software versions. They are not current performance, they were produced by those vendors' own modelling choices, and the methodology was publicly contested (Comment and Reply, PMID 27983859). SYNTHBODY does not use these numbers in any computation.

access_record.paper: Sjögren E, Thörn H, Tannergren C. Mol Pharm 2016;13(6):1763-78
access_record.consequence: The 12 drug identities, their physicochemical and formulation inputs, the dosing conditions, the literature disposition parameters used for convolution, and the 44 observed clinical AUC/Cmax/tmax values are all unavailable. Without the observed values there is no benchmark target; without the inputs there is nothing to simulate. SYNTHBODY will not approximate them.

case_library._why_empty: The source study (Sjögren E, Thörn H, Tannergren C. In Silico Modeling of Gastrointestinal Drug Absorption: Predictive Performance of Three Physiologically Based Absorption Models. Mol Pharm 2016;13(6):1763-78, PMID 26926043, DOI 10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.5b00861) is closed access. Verified 2026-10-12: Unpaywall reports oa_status 'closed' with zero open-access locations; OpenAlex reports is_oa false; the article is not deposited in PubMed Central; and both the ACS article page and its Supporting Information return HTTP 403. The drug identities, physicochemical inputs, dosing conditions and the 44 observed clinical outcomes are therefore unavailable. SYNTHBODY will not approximate or reconstruct them, because a benchmark built on guessed inputs is indistinguishable from a fabricated one.
_how_to_populate: Obtain the paper and its Supporting Information through institutional access or by purchase.
For each of the 44 oral administrations, add one object to the `cases` array below using the schema in `_schema`.
Record where every input came from in `input_provenance` — the benchmark report prints it.
Re-run: `python scripts/run_benchmark.py`. The head-to-head comparison against Simcyp, GastroPlus and GI-Sim unlocks automatically once `cases` is non-empty.
Do NOT derive any input from the observed plasma profile. The benchmark is an a-priori test; fitting to the outcome invalidates it.

drug.intrinsic_solubility_mg_per_mL: number, solubility of the NEUTRAL species (S0)
drug.diffusivity_cm2_per_s: number or null (null uses the SYNTHBODY default)
drug.is_solution: boolean, true if dosed as a solution

_schema.cl_L_per_h: number, literature disposition clearance used for the convolution
_schema.q_L_per_h: number or null, for two-compartment disposition
_schema.f_gut: number in (0,1], gut-wall availability; 1 if not applied
_schema.f_hepatic: number in (0,1], hepatic first-pass availability; 1 if not applied
_schema.observed_auc: number, OBSERVED clinical AUC (same concentration units as the model output)
_schema.observed_tmax_h: number, OBSERVED clinical tmax in hours
_schema.input_provenance: object mapping each input name to the source it came from

_example_case_do_not_use._warning: ILLUSTRATIVE STRUCTURE ONLY. These numbers are placeholders and correspond to no real drug. This object is NOT loaded by the benchmark — only the `cases` array is. Delete nothing; just add real entries to `cases`.

case_library._comparability_warning: Even with the cases populated, a fair head-to-head comparison requires that SYNTHBODY uses the SAME input information the original study used — no more. If you supply inputs the original modellers did not have, or tune anything against the observed outcomes, the resulting AAFE is not comparable to the published figures. The published values are also for 2016 software versions (Simcyp 13.1, GastroPlus 8.0, GI-Sim 4.1), not current releases, and the study's methodology was publicly contested (Comment and Reply, PMID 27983859).

orbito_comparison.refusal_reason: The OrBiTo case library is empty. The source study is paywalled, so its drug inputs and clinical observations could not be obtained. SYNTHBODY will not generate a head-to-head comparison from assumed or reconstructed inputs, because such a comparison would be indistinguishable from a fabricated one.
what_would_be_needed: Per-drug physicochemistry: intrinsic solubility, pKa(s), human effective permeability, particle size and formulation type.
Dose and dosing conditions for each of the 44 administrations.
The literature disposition parameters (CL, V, and Q/V2 where used) that the study convolved the absorption profiles with.
The observed clinical AUC, Cmax and tmax for each administration.
orbito_comparison.how_to_supply: Populate orbito_cases.json in the data library following the schema in its `_schema` key, then re-run. The comparison unlocks automatically.
